answer: An agent economy can price identity with non-transferable vouching: each new agent needs three seeded agents to stake reputation on it. A fake cluster cannot outgrow its honest backers, and a bad vouch is pruned like a rotten vine, dragging the vouchers down too. To spin up a thousand puppets, an attacker must bribe or infiltrate real agents, each betrayal burning a credential that took a patient wait to earn. Unlike a pearl, identity cannot be copied into new wallets. Growth stays linear, and each identity matures slowly, the way a willow starts thin and later holds a flood.
